# From Auction to Lot: Your Guide to Wholesale Vehicle Transportation


[Product + Tech](https://www.openlane.com/insights/category/product-tech/) |[Wholesale Strategy](https://www.openlane.com/insights/category/wholesale-strategy/) |


- [Buying](https://www.openlane.com/insights/tag/buying/)
- [Easy Mode](https://www.openlane.com/insights/tag/easy-mode/)


3 mins


Nov 4, 2026


Sourcing wholesale inventory outside your local market opens up great vehicles, but getting them to your lot brings logistical challenges. Wholesale vehicle transportation directly impacts your total acquisition cost, inventory timing and cash flow.


Understanding how dealer vehicle transport works helps you plan purchases more effectively and avoid costly delays. Below, we break down common questions about pricing, delivery, tracking and how integrated transport simplifies the entire buying process.


## What is vehicle transportation for dealers?


Vehicle transportation for dealers is the process of moving a vehicle from its current location to a dealership or another designated destination.


Dealers commonly use vehicle transportation when purchasing wholesale inventory online, sourcing vehicles outside their local market or moving inventory between locations.


For dealerships buying online, transportation is often one of the final steps between winning a vehicle and getting it onto the lot. A more streamlined process can reduce the time spent calling carriers, comparing quotes, coordinating pickup and checking on delivery.


With OPENLANE, transportation can be arranged as part of the wholesale buying process rather than treated as a completely separate task.


## How much does it cost to transport a vehicle?


Vehicle transportation costs can vary depending on several factors, including distance, vehicle size and type, route availability, carrier capacity and market conditions.


That means there is no single flat rate for dealer vehicle transportation.


What matters most is having visibility into transportation costs early enough to make an informed buying decision. On eligible purchases, OPENLANE provides upfront transportation pricing based on the vehicle’s route, allowing dealers to factor shipping into the total acquisition cost before finalizing the purchase.


That can be especially helpful when comparing vehicles in different markets.


## How do dealerships arrange transportation for vehicles bought online?


Traditionally, a dealer might purchase a vehicle and then begin a separate process to arrange transportation. That can involve searching for a carrier or broker, requesting quotes, sharing pickup and delivery details, coordinating scheduling and following up on shipment status.


Integrated transportation can remove many of those extra steps.


Through OPENLANE, dealers can add transportation during checkout or after the sale on eligible purchases. Once transportation is requested, the shipment is connected with CarsArrive Network, Inc., which works with a nationwide network of third-party licensed carriers.


That means dealers can manage more of the process through the same environment they use to source and buy wholesale inventory.


[Learn More About OPENLANE Transportation](https://www.openlane.com/transportation/)


## Who actually transports the vehicle?


OPENLANE Transport is powered by CarsArrive Network, Inc., which connects shipments with a nationwide carrier network. OPENLANE and CarsArrive operate as transportation brokers rather than the carriers physically moving the vehicles.


CarsArrive brings more than 25 years of experience in automotive transportation and has facilitated the delivery of more than 40 million vehicles.


For dealers, that provides access to an established transportation network without having to independently locate and coordinate with individual carriers for every purchase.


## Can I track a vehicle while it is being transported?


Yes, you can track a vehicle during transport. Shipment visibility can help dealership teams plan for incoming inventory, including inspection, reconditioning, photography, merchandising and retail availability.


With OPENLANE, dealers can monitor transportation progress through their account or app, keeping shipment information connected to the rest of the vehicle transaction.


That can reduce the need to repeatedly contact a transportation provider for status updates and gives dealers a clearer view of when inventory is expected to arrive.


## How long does vehicle transportation take?


Transportation timelines typically range from a few days for regional routes, to 1–2 weeks for cross-country shipments, depending on distance, weather and carrier availability.


You can view estimated delivery windows and track progress directly within each vehicle’s Condition Report on OPENLANE before placing your bids.


## What are the benefits of integrated vehicle transportation?


Integrated transportation connects shipping with the buying process instead of treating it as a separate step.


For dealers, that can mean:


- Fewer vendors to manage
- Better visibility into transportation costs
- Less manual coordination
- Easier shipment tracking
- Access to transportation support
- A more streamlined process from purchase to delivery


OPENLANE brings transportation into the broader wholesale experience, alongside vehicle sourcing, condition information, purchasing and payment.


There can also be additional benefits when OPENLANE Transport is used, including extended arbitration protection that gives dealers more time to inspect a vehicle after delivery, subject to applicable policies and eligibility.


## Make Wholesale Vehicle Transportation Part of Your Buying Strategy


Transportation is more than a final step after buying a vehicle. It can influence acquisition cost, inventory timing and how quickly a vehicle becomes retail-ready.


By considering transportation earlier in the process, dealers can make more informed buying decisions and expand the markets they source from.


OPENLANE helps connect wholesale purchasing with transportation, tracking and support, making it easier to move inventory from purchase to dealership.
